title: Sodom and the Son of Promise, part 3 of 6: Isaac Is Born, Hagar and Ishmael Sent Away
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The age of the patriarchs in the ancient Near East, about four thousand years ago: people dressed in simple garments of wool or linen, undyed or dyed in earth colours, tents of black goat hair, tools of wood, stone and bronze, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

ABRAHAM.name: Abraham
ABRAHAM.desc: Abraham, a tall, upright old man who looks about eighty and is still strong, with warm brown, deeply weathered and lined skin, thick wavy white hair reaching his collar, a full white beard, white eyebrows, a strong straight nose and steady, thoughtful dark eyes, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved tunic of undyed cream wool with a brown leather belt and a deep russet-red wool mantle draped over his left shoulder, and simple leather sandals

SARAH.name: Sarah
SARAH.desc: Sarah, a graceful, dignified old woman who looks about seventy and is still beautiful, with warm brown skin finely lined at the eyes and mouth, large dark eyes, high cheekbones and long wavy silver-grey hair, her hair mostly covered by a long indigo-blue wool head shawl that falls over her shoulders, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved dress of undyed cream wool with a woven belt of red and blue, and simple leather sandals

ISHMAEL.name: Ishmael
ISHMAEL.desc: Ishmael, a lean, wiry boy of thirteen, beardless, with reddish-brown sun-browned skin, large dark almond-shaped eyes, a narrow face with a small pointed chin, a straight nose and thick wavy black hair falling to the nape of his neck, wearing a knee-length short-sleeved tunic of undyed cream wool tied at the waist with a narrow faded green cloth sash, and simple leather sandals

HAGAR.name: Hagar
HAGAR.desc: Hagar, a slender young Egyptian woman of about twenty-five, with reddish-brown skin, large dark almond-shaped eyes, a narrow face with a small pointed chin, and straight black hair cut level at the shoulders with a straight fringe across her forehead, wearing no head shawl, in an ankle-length long-sleeved servant's dress of plain sand-brown wool tied at the waist with a narrow faded green cloth sash, a thin copper bracelet on her left wrist, and simple leather sandals

ABIMELECH.name: Abimelech
ABIMELECH.desc: Abimelech, the king of Gerar, a broad-shouldered man of about forty-five with warm olive-brown skin, a square face, heavy black eyebrows, deep-set dark eyes, wavy black hair reaching his shoulders and a full black beard trimmed square with a little grey at the chin, wearing a thin plain gold band around his head, an ankle-length long-sleeved robe of madder-red wool with a woven border of dark blue and cream at the hem and cuffs, a wide belt of brown leather, a dark green fringed wool mantle wrapped over his right shoulder, and leather sandals

HAGAR_OLDER.name: Hagar
HAGAR_OLDER.desc: Hagar, a slender Egyptian woman of about forty, with reddish-brown skin, fine lines at the corners of her eyes and mouth, large dark almond-shaped eyes, a narrow face with a small pointed chin, and straight black hair with a few grey strands cut level at the shoulders with a straight fringe across her forehead, wearing no head shawl, in an ankle-length long-sleeved servant's dress of plain sand-brown wool tied at the waist with a narrow faded green cloth sash, a thin copper bracelet on her left wrist, and simple leather sandals

ISHMAEL_MAN.name: Ishmael
ISHMAEL_MAN.desc: Ishmael as a grown man of about twenty-five, lean, wiry and sun-hardened, with reddish-brown sun-browned skin, large dark almond-shaped eyes, a narrow face with a small pointed chin, a straight nose, thick wavy black hair falling to the nape of his neck and a short black beard, wearing a knee-length short-sleeved tunic of undyed cream wool tied at the waist with a narrow faded green cloth sash, a plain leather quiver of arrows slung on his back, and simple leather sandals

PHICOL.name: Phicol
PHICOL.desc: Phicol, the commander of Abimelech's army, a tall, lean, hard-faced man of about fifty with warm olive-brown skin, a hooked nose, a pale scar through his left eyebrow, close-cropped iron-grey hair and a short iron-grey beard, wearing a plain brown leather headband, a knee-length short-sleeved tunic of dark blue wool with a red woven border, a broad brown leather belt with a short bronze dagger in a leather sheath, a leather guard on each forearm, a plain brown wool cloak pinned at his right shoulder, and leather sandals; no helmet and no armour

segs.text: Now the LORD attended to Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what He had promised.
So Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised.
And Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore to him.
When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God had commanded him.
Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
Then Sarah said,
God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me.
She added,
Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.
So the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking her son,
and she said to Abraham,
Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac!
Now this matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son Ishmael.
But God said to Abraham,
Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant. Listen to everything that Sarah tells you, for through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.
But I will also make a nation of the slave woman’s son, because he is your offspring.
Early in the morning, Abraham got up, took bread and a skin of water, put them on Hagar’s shoulders, and sent her away with the boy. She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.
When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes.
Then she went off and sat down nearby, about a bowshot away, for she said,
I cannot bear to watch the boy die!
And as she sat nearby, she lifted up her voice and wept.
Then God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven,
What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.
Get up, lift up the boy, and take him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation.
Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
And God was with the boy, and he grew up and settled in the wilderness and became a great archer.
And while he was dwelling in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother got a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
At that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army said to Abraham,
God is with you in all that you do.

Now, therefore, swear to me here before God that you will not deal falsely with me or my children or descendants. Show to me and to the country in which you reside the same kindness that I have shown to you.
And Abraham replied,
I swear it.
But when Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well that Abimelech’s servants had seized,
Abimelech replied,
I do not know who has done this. You did not tell me, so I have not heard about it until today.
So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a covenant.
Abraham separated seven ewe lambs from the flock,
and Abimelech asked him,
Why have you set apart these seven ewe lambs?
He replied,
You are to accept the seven ewe lambs from my hand as my witness that I dug this well.
So that place was called Beersheba, because it was there that the two of them swore an oath.
After they had made the covenant at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.
And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.
And Abraham resided in the land of the Philistines for a long time.

{EMPTY}. Sunrise over {GCAMP}. The tents are quiet, a flock of sheep lies resting beside them and the low sun throws long golden light across the grass. Seen from a little above. No smoke. Wide view.

The LORD attended to Sarah: {SARAH}, stands alone in front of {TENT}, in early morning, her face lifted and her eyes closed, one hand laid flat on her waist and the other at her heart, while a soft radiance of pure golden-white light pours down on her from above the frame. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {ONE}. {NOHALO}. Medium view.

So Sarah conceived: {SARAH}, walks slowly through dry golden grass beside black tents; she is with child, her belly clearly rounded under her cream dress, and one of her hands rests on it. Beside her walks {ABRAHAM}, his hand under her elbow, looking at her with wonder. {TWO}. Medium view.

Night in a camp of black goat-hair tents on dry grassland under a sky full of stars. The largest tent glows warm gold from a lamp inside, its door flap closed. Two serving women in plain wool dresses and head shawls hurry toward it, one carrying a clay water jar and the other an armful of folded cloths. Exactly two people, both women, seen small from a distance. Wide view.

She bore a son to Abraham in his old age: {INTENT}. {SARAH}, lies propped on cushions under a striped wool blanket drawn up to her shoulders, tired and radiant, holding against her shoulder {BABY}. Beside the bed kneels {ABRAHAM}, one hand pressed over his mouth in wonder, his eyes wet. Two adults and one baby, no one else. Medium view.

Abraham gave the name Isaac to his son: at the door of a black goat-hair tent in clear morning light, {ABRAHAM}, holds up in both his hands, level with his own face, {BABY}, and looks into the child's face, speaking his name with a broad, gentle smile. One man and one baby, no one else. {NOHALO}. Medium close view.

Very close view of things laid ready on a woven wool rug inside a tent: {FLINT}, lying on a square of folded clean white linen, beside a small clay bowl of water and a little clay jar of olive oil. Soft morning light from the tent door. {NOPEOPLE}. No blood. Close view.

On the eighth day, as God had commanded him: in front of {TENT}, in morning light, {ABRAHAM}, stands holding close against his chest {BABY}, his head bowed over the child and his face grave and tender. A few {HERDSMEN}, stand at a respectful distance behind him, watching quietly. Everyone is fully clothed. No knife in the picture, no blood. Medium view.

Very close view: the tiny hand of a newborn baby with warm brown skin grips one finger of an old man's large, weathered, deeply lined brown hand, lying on undyed cream wool cloth. Warm lamplight. Only the two hands are in the frame, no faces. Close view.

God has made me laugh: close view of {SARAH}, laughing out loud with joy, her head tilted a little back and her eyes creased, holding in her arms {BABY}. Only her head, shoulders and the baby are in the frame, the dark tent cloth behind. One woman and one baby, no one else. {NOHALO}. Close view.

Everyone who hears of this will laugh with me: in the shade in front of a black goat-hair tent, {SARAH}, sits on a rug holding {BABY}, and around her sit and kneel four {WOMEN}, all laughing with her, one clapping her hands and one wiping her eyes. Five women and one baby, no men. Medium wide view.

Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? {SARAH}, sits inside a tent in soft daylight from the door, looking down in wonder at {BABY}, who lies in the crook of her arm, and touches his cheek with one fingertip. One woman and one baby, no one else. Fully clothed. Medium close view.

I have borne him a son in his old age: in the open door of a black goat-hair tent, {ABRAHAM}, sits on a low stool with {BABY}, asleep in the crook of his arm, gazing down at him; behind his shoulder stands {SARAH}, her hand on his shoulder, smiling down at them both. Two adults and one baby, no one else. Medium view.

So the child grew: on dry golden grass in front of black tents, {CHILD}, takes unsteady steps forward, holding on with one small hand to two fingers of {SARAH}, who stoops beside him, watching his feet and smiling. One woman and one small child, no one else. Medium view.

Abraham held a great feast: dusk in a camp of black goat-hair tents on dry grassland. A great crowd of men, women and children of the household, in simple wool tunics, dresses and head shawls, sits on woven rugs in a wide ring around a cooking fire, with flat round loaves of bread, roast meat on wooden platters and clay bowls and jars set out on the rugs between them; serving women carry more platters. Small clay lamps burn among the rugs. No tables, no chairs, no benches. Wide view from a little above.

On the day Isaac was weaned: in the firelight of the feast, {ABRAHAM}, lifts high above his head in both hands {CHILD}, who laughs down at him, while seated feasters behind them, in simple wool clothes, look up and clap. Medium view from low down.

The son of Hagar was mocking her son: at the firelit edge of the feast two boys are alone. On the left stands {ISHMAEL}; he is tall and lean, nearly grown, laughing scornfully with his head cocked and his lip curled, pointing down with one finger at the small child in front of him. On the right, sitting on a rug and looking up at him with a puzzled, hurt face and a piece of bread in his hand, is {CHILD}. Exactly two people: one beardless youth and one little child of three, no one else. He does not touch the child. Medium view.

But Sarah saw: close view of the face of {SARAH}, lit from one side by firelight at dusk, her smile gone, her eyes narrowed and fixed on something off to the right of the picture, her mouth set hard. Only her head and shoulders are in the frame. {ONE}. Close view.

Hagar the Egyptian: at the edge of the feast at dusk, {HAGAR_OLDER}, stands holding a wooden platter of flat bread in both hands; she has stopped still and looks across the firelight with a worried face, as a mother who sees trouble coming. Seated feasters in wool clothes are dim shapes behind her. Medium view.

Expel the slave woman and her son! {INTENT}, at night. {SARAH}, stands facing {ABRAHAM}, her arm stretched out pointing toward the open tent door and the dark outside, her face fierce, speaking; he stands with his hands half raised and open, dismayed. {TWO}. No one strikes anyone. Medium view.

The slave woman and her son: at night beside the glowing embers of a burnt-down fire, with dark tents behind, {HAGAR_OLDER}, sits on the ground handing a piece of flat bread to {ISHMAEL}, who sits cross-legged beside her, a tall youth, nearly grown. Neither knows that anything is wrong. {MOTHERSON}. Medium view.

My son Isaac: inside a lamplit tent, close view of {SARAH}, holding against her shoulder the sleeping {CHILD}, one of her hands spread over the back of his curly head, her face set and resolved as she looks straight ahead. One woman and one small child, no one else. Close view.

This matter distressed Abraham greatly: night on dry grassland outside the camp. {ABRAHAM}, sits alone on a low rock, bent forward with his forehead in one hand and his other hand hanging between his knees, his face creased with grief. Dark tents far behind him under {STARS}. {ONE}. Medium view.

Because it concerned his son Ishmael: at night {ABRAHAM}, stands in the dark on the left, looking down with a sorrowful face at {ISHMAEL}, who lies asleep on his side on the ground at the right, under a striped wool blanket beside faintly glowing embers, a tall youth, nearly grown. {MANBOY}. Medium view.

But God said to Abraham: night on open dry grassland. {GLORY}, floods the grass in front of an old man. {ABRAHAM}, is seen from behind and a little to one side, small in the lower left of the picture, risen to his feet from a low rock and looking up into the light. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {ONE}. Wide view.

Do not be distressed: close view of the face of {ABRAHAM}, lit from above and in front by a strong golden-white light from outside the picture, tears on his cheeks, his brow slowly easing as he listens. Only his head and shoulders are in the frame, with the dark night behind. {ONE}. {NOEYES}. {NOHALO}. Close view.

Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned: inside a dark tent at night, {CHILD}, lies asleep on a sheepskin under a small wool blanket, one small hand by his cheek, while a soft shaft of golden-white light from above the frame falls across him. One small sleeping child, no one else. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOHALO}. Close view.

I will also make a nation of the slave woman's son. {VISION}. A wide desert plain holding a great camp of many dark tents, with herds of camels and a crowd of tiny people, some of them carrying bows, stretching away to bare mountains under a huge glowing sky. No buildings, no banners, no writing. Very wide view.

Early in the morning, Abraham got up: in the grey light before sunrise, {ABRAHAM}, comes out of {TENT}, holding the door flap aside with one hand, his face tired and grave after a sleepless night. The camp behind him is still asleep. {ONE}. Medium view.

He took bread and a skin of water: very close view of an old man's weathered brown hands, in cream wool sleeves, wrapping a stack of flat round loaves of bread in a square of plain cloth, on a woven rug beside a full, bulging {SKIN}. Grey early light. {HANDS}. Close view.

He put them on Hagar's shoulders: at dawn at the edge of a camp of black tents, three people stand. From left to right they are: {ABRAHAM}, who is settling the strap of a full dark-brown goat-hide water skin onto the woman's shoulder with both hands; then {HAGAR_OLDER}, in the middle, standing still with a cloth bundle of bread tied on her other shoulder and her eyes lowered; then {ISHMAEL}, at the right, a tall youth, nearly grown, looking at the old man with a bewildered face. {THREEP}: one old man, one woman and one youth. Medium view.

At dawn, {ABRAHAM}, stands with both his hands laid on the shoulders of {ISHMAEL}, a tall youth, nearly grown, who stands facing him; the old man's head is bowed toward the boy and his eyes are shut in grief, and the boy looks down at the ground. Seen in side view against a pale dawn sky and dry grassland. {MANBOY}. Medium close view.

And sent her away with the boy: sunrise over wide, empty dry grassland. In the foreground on the left stands {ABRAHAM}, seen from behind, his arms hanging at his sides. Far ahead of him two small figures seen from behind walk away into the open land: a woman in a sand-brown dress carrying a dark water skin on her shoulder and a lean youth in a cream tunic beside her. {THREEP}. No animals, no tents ahead of them. Wide view.

She wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba: seen from high above and far away, {WILD}. Two tiny figures cross the empty land with long shadows, a woman in a sand-brown dress and a youth in a cream tunic, following no path. Exactly two tiny people, no one else, no animals. Very wide view.

When the water in the skin was gone: under a white midday sun in {WILD}, {HAGAR_OLDER}, kneels on the stony ground holding a limp, flat, empty dark-brown goat-hide water skin upside down in both hands and stares at its dry mouth; beside her {ISHMAEL}, a tall youth, nearly grown, has sunk down sitting with his head hanging and his lips cracked. Both are grey with dust. {MOTHERSON}. Medium view.

She left the boy under one of the bushes: in {WILD}, {ISHMAEL}, a tall youth, nearly grown, lies on his side on the ground with his eyes closed and his lips cracked, in the thin shade under {BUSH}. Kneeling over him, {HAGAR_OLDER}, draws her hand slowly away from his hair, her face stricken. {MOTHERSON}. Medium view.

She sat down nearby, about a bowshot away: very wide view of {WILD}. Far away on the left edge of the picture a youth in a cream tunic lies very small under a grey-green bush. Far from him, on the right side of the picture and nearer to us, a woman in a sand-brown dress sits on the ground with her back turned to him and her face in her hands. A wide stretch of empty stony ground lies between them. Exactly two people, far apart, no one else, no animals. Very wide view.

I cannot bear to watch the boy die! Close view of {HAGAR_OLDER}, sitting on stony desert ground with her face turned away over her shoulder from something behind her, her eyes squeezed shut and one dusty hand half covering her face, her lips parted as she speaks. Only her head, shoulders and hand are in the frame; pale empty desert behind. {ONE}. Close view.

She lifted up her voice and wept: {HAGAR_OLDER}, sits alone on the stony ground of {WILD}, her face lifted to the empty sky and her mouth open in a cry, tears running through the dust on her cheeks, her hands lying open and helpless in her lap, the empty flat water skin on the ground beside her. {ONE}. Medium view.

God heard the voice of the boy: close view of {ISHMAEL}, a tall youth, nearly grown, lying on his side on stony ground under the thin grey-green twigs of a desert bush, his cheek on his arm, his eyes half open and his cracked lips parted as he whispers. Only his head, shoulder and arm are in the frame. {ONE}. Close view.

The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven: very wide view of {WILD}. {SKYLIGHT}. Far below, very small, a woman in a sand-brown dress sitting on the ground has thrown her head back to look straight up into it. Exactly one tiny person. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Very wide view.

What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid: close view of the face of {HAGAR_OLDER}, lifted toward the sky and lit from above by a strong golden-white light from outside the picture, her eyes wide, her lips parted, tears still wet on her dusty cheeks. Only her head and shoulders are in the frame. {ONE}. {HEREYES}. {NOHALO}. Close view.

God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies: in the desert a soft shaft of golden-white light from above the frame falls on {BUSH}, and on a lean youth in a cream wool tunic with a faded green sash who lies on his side beneath it with his eyes closed. Exactly one person. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOHALO}. Medium view.

Get up: in {WILD}, {HAGAR_OLDER}, has sprung to her feet and runs across the stony ground from left to right, her dress and hair flying, her eyes fixed ahead on a grey-green bush in the distance at the right, golden-white light falling on the ground from above. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium wide view in side view.

Lift up the boy, and take him by the hand: beside a desert bush, {HAGAR_OLDER}, kneels with one arm round the back of {ISHMAEL}, a tall youth, nearly grown, whom she has raised to sit up against her, and her other hand grips his hand tightly; his eyes are just opening. {MOTHERSON}. Medium close view.

card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 21:1–34, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 21:1-34 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, S Sarah (21:6-7, 21:10), G the voice of God (21:12-13), H Hagar (21:16), L the angel of God (21:17-18; same voice as the angel of the LORD in s02e01d and as G, a default that can be changed at assembly), K Abimelech (21:22-23, 21:26, 21:29; the text gives the words of 21:22-23 to 'Abimelech and Phicol', spoken here by the king alone), A Abraham (21:24, 21:30).
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. REF = character reference sheet (not used in the film, no clip). Still 'verses' are chapter:verse.

Faces: Abraham and Sarah use the aged sheets of s02e01e (description text word for word); Abraham is a hundred (21:5). Ishmael uses refs/REF-ISHMAEL.jpg (made for 17:25, age thirteen) with its text word for word plus 'a tall youth, nearly grown': by the text's own numbers he is about sixteen at the weaning (17:25, 21:5, 21:8; that Isaac was weaned at about three is I). Abimelech uses refs/REF-ABIMELECH.jpg from s02e02b.

New sheets in this unit: refs/REF-HAGAR-OLDER.jpg (key HAGAR_OLDER), Hagar about sixteen years after Genesis 16, derived from refs/REF-HAGAR.jpg (same woman, about forty, a few grey strands; I); refs/REF-ISHMAEL-MAN.jpg (key ISHMAEL_MAN), Ishmael as a bearded man of about twenty-five with a quiver, derived from refs/REF-ISHMAEL.jpg (21:20-21; reusable at 25:9); refs/REF-PHICOL.jpg (key PHICOL), the commander of Abimelech's army (21:22, 21:32; his looks are I: no helmet or armour, dressed like the men of Gerar in s02e02b). Isaac has no sheet here: BABY (newborn, swaddled) and CHILD (about three) are description blocks; Genesis 22 designs him as a youth. The Egyptian wife of 21:21 has a description block only (BRIDE).

Place: after Genesis 20 Abraham lives in the land of Gerar (20:15) and the chapter ends at Beersheba, so the camp is painted on dry grassland by a dry stream bed (block GCAMP), not under the oaks of Mamre (I). 'The land of the Philistines' (21:32, 21:34) is painted as that same grassland; no Aegean or feathered-headdress dress is used, and whether the name is a later one for the region is not decided on screen.

God is light only (GLORY, golden-white light from above the frame). 21:1 'the LORD attended to Sarah' is light on Sarah (A2). 21:12-13: God speaks to Abraham at night (the hour is I, from 21:14 'early in the morning'). 21:17 'the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven' is a shaft of light from the open sky (block SKYLIGHT): no figure, face or wings; whether the angel is God himself or a messenger is not resolved. The promises of 21:13 and 21:18 are one faceless vision (M1, block VISION).

21:2 the birth is not shown: a lamplit closed tent at night with women bringing water and cloths (B2, I), then Sarah with the swaddled child (B3). 21:4 nothing of the circumcision is shown: a flint knife on linen (D1; flint is I, from Exodus 4:25 and Joshua 5:2-3) and Abraham holding the wrapped child (D2). 21:7 'nurse children' is pictured only as Sarah holding the wrapped baby; nothing bare.

21:9 follows the BSB main text, 'was mocking her son': Ishmael laughs and points at the small Isaac and does not touch him (I1). What the mocking was is disputed (the Hebrew word is the 'laugh' of Isaac's name; Galatians 4:29 calls it persecution) and the picture shows no more than scornful laughter. I3 (Hagar watching, worried) and J2 (Hagar and Ishmael by the embers, unaware) are I.

21:14: the bread and the water skin are put on Hagar's shoulders (BSB); Ishmael walks beside her and is never carried. N4 (Abraham's hands on Ishmael's shoulders) is D: the text records no farewell, only that the matter distressed him greatly (21:11). 21:15 'she left the boy under one of the bushes': she lays the fainting youth in the shade of a desert broom bush (the kind of bush is I). 21:16 'about a bowshot away' is a wide stretch of empty ground between them (P2). 21:17 'God heard the voice of the boy': the boy whispers under the bush (Q1); the text does not give his words.

21:19: the well is an ordinary stone-ringed well in a hollow that she had not seen (S2); it does not spring up. 21:20-21: Ishmael the archer looses one arrow at nothing seen (T3); no kill is shown. Paran is painted as bare red-brown mountain desert (I); his wife is led to him by Hagar's hand (U2; no rite is described).

21:22-32: everyone is on foot. 21:25 'a well that Abimelech's servants had seized' is three men of Gerar barring the well with staffs (Y2, I); no blow. Z2 (the king questioning Phicol) is I. 21:27 'made a covenant' is a clasp of right forearms (AA2, I: the text describes no rite, and no animals are cut). 21:28 AB1 must show exactly seven lambs; elsewhere the lambs are shown only in part so that no other number can be counted. 21:31 the oath is two raised right hands across the well (AE1, I). Which well it is and where Beersheba lay is not marked.
21:33: the tamarisk is planted as a waist-high sapling beside the well (AG1); AH1 shows the same tree full-grown for 'a long time' (21:34, I). No altar is shown, since the text names none here.
Narration is not generated in this unit; shots are laid at assembly.
